close.note: Scope stays open. Sprint 2 delivered the completion/reopen lifecycle and its adversarial gates; decide explicitly whether the scope objective is met before completing it.
close.summary: Explicit scope completion and reopen replace inferred terminal states; verification replays lifecycle transitions instead of trusting records.
recommendations: Before completing this scope, verify each success criterion against evidence rather than treating all-tasks-done as proof the objective was met.
If further lifecycle transitions are added (e.g. suspend/resume), extend checkpoints/lifecycle-state.ts and its replay first, then the command surface.
learnings: Adding a lawful post-close state transition is incomplete until the integrity lens learns to replay it — completion (T2.2) silently left every completed scope reading as DIVERGED until reopen forced the checkpoint verifier to be taught the transition.
Sharing one set of after-state builders between the writers and the verifier removes a whole class of drift: the verifier cannot disagree with the writer about what a lawful transition produces.

beforeClose.title: Adaptive sprint lifecycle
beforeClose.objective: Make Kyro record changing work truthfully without treating a partial sprint or exhausted roadmap as a terminal scope failure.
successCriteria: Every unfinished task has a typed, reasoned disposition before sprint closure.
Closing any sprint preserves immutable evidence while keeping the scope open for explicit next planning.
Scope completion and retirement remain explicit, distinct decisions.
Doctor and Integrity distinguish lawful lifecycle evolution from immutable-artifact corruption.
Legacy checkpoints remain readable without retroactive semantic claims.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL require an explicit validated disposition for every unfinished task before closing a sprint.
requirements.rationale: Unfinished work must remain discoverable and attributable instead of being represented as success or silently discarded.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL close a sprint without automatically completing its scope merely because all originally planned roadmap entries are closed.
requirements.rationale: A roadmap is an estimate; scope completion requires an explicit decision and evidence.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL allow an open scope with no active sprint to plan a subsequent sprint through the normal tool-owned flow.
requirements.rationale: Legitimate reprioritization must not require a recovery or manual state edit.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL preserve fail-closed validation for immutable checkpoints, unsafe paths, identity conflicts, and stale approvals while accepting lawful lifecycle evolution.
requirements.rationale: Simplification must not weaken artifact integrity or recovery safety.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL keep retirement distinct from scope completion and preserve readable historical checkpoint semantics.
requirements.rationale: Terminal retirement has explicit human approval semantics, and immutable historical bytes cannot be rewritten.

scenarios.given: an active sprint has unfinished tasks
scenarios.then: each unfinished task must carry a valid explicit disposition with its reason and any required continuation reference

scenarios.given: the final originally planned sprint has a mixture of completed and disposed tasks
scenarios.then: the immutable close record reports a truthful partial outcome and the scope is not automatically completed

scenarios.given: an open scope has closed all originally listed roadmap sprints
scenarios.when: the user supplies a later sprint plan
scenarios.then: kyro plan materializes it through the normal tool-owned route without recovery

scenarios.given: a scope contains either lawful lifecycle evolution or an unsafe/corrupt immutable artifact
scenarios.then: lawful evolution is distinguishable from scoped fail-closed artifact corruption

scenarios.given: a historical or retired scope is inspected
scenarios.then: historical records remain readable and retirement remains explicitly terminal and human-gated

scenarios.given: an open scope has no active sprint, no unresolved debt or review, and healthy artifacts
scenarios.when: the user explicitly confirms scope completion
scenarios.then: Kyro records completion as a distinct lifecycle fact without retiring the scope or rewriting its archive

scenarios.given: a completed but non-retired scope needs later work
scenarios.when: the user explicitly reopens it with a reason
scenarios.then: Kyro preserves completion history and routes the scope to plan_sprint without recovery or manual edits

nonGoals: Startup-contract consolidation or unrelated global preflight redesign.
NutriLens or Kyro Lens implementation changes.
Manual editing mode for Kyro-managed state.
Archive rewriting, release, installation, publication, or version bump.

conventions.rule: A post-close live-state transition is valid only if it replays exactly from the checkpoint after-image through the same builders the writer uses; lifecycle records are evidence, never authority.

roadmap.sizingRationale: The work is sequenced by semantic dependency: define the lifecycle contract first, implement the core transitions second, then reconcile integrity and certify the complete path.

phases.title: Explicit scope-completion contract
phases.objective: Define and implement a minimal tool-owned completion statement distinct from retirement.

tasks.title: Model explicit scope completion and historical compatibility
tasks.description: Add the smallest typed completion record and derived-status rules so completed, retired, and still-open scopes have distinct, truthful meanings without rewriting legacy checkpoints.
tasks.context: Completion must be a positive tool-owned statement. Roadmap exhaustion and a closed sprint are insufficient. Preserve legacy nextAction=done reads without retroactively inventing completion metadata.
acceptance_criteria: A new scope-completion record is validated and distinguishable from retirement.
Derived status marks a new scope completed only from explicit completion or retirement, while legacy terminal records remain readable.
Malformed or contradictory completion metadata is rejected without writes.

evidence.summary: Modeled explicit scope completion as a typed, tool-owned record distinct from retirement: added ScopeCompletion and SprintFile.completion / KyroScopeEntry.completion; schema validation rejects malformed completion and completion+retirement coexistence (both on sprint.json and project-state scope entries) and requires status=completed, activeSprint=null, nextAction=done; deriveScopeStatus now marks completed only from explicit completion, retirement, or a legacy done handoff (readable), never from roadmap exhaustion; added COMPLETION_CONFLICT error code; added T2.1 regression coverage in check-status.mjs (derivation, validation, legacy read, entry validation).

checked_criteria: A new scope-completion record is validated and distinguishable from retirement.
Derived status marks a new scope completed only from explicit completion or retirement, while legacy terminal records remain readable.
Malformed or contradictory completion metadata is rejected without writes.

tasks.title: Implement guarded scope completion
tasks.description: Extend the existing scope command with an explicit completion transition that validates readiness, writes only tool-owned lifecycle state, and requires deliberate confirmation.
tasks.context: Use a scope subcommand, not a new root verb. Refuse active work, debt, pending review, artifact divergence, and stale confirmation. Completion must not create or masquerade as a retirement checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: An eligible open scope can be explicitly completed only through the dedicated tool-owned scope transition with confirmation.
The transition refuses non-ready or divergent scopes with no state write.
Completion is visible in status and context-pack and remains structurally distinct from retirement.

evidence.summary: Implemented guarded scope completion via a new 'kyro scope complete' subcommand (distinct from retirement): validates readiness (no active sprint, no open debt, no review debt, no blocking findings, healthy close checkpoints), requires deliberate confirmation (scope_complete policy guard at confirm level), writes only tool-owned lifecycle state (sprint.json completion record + project-state scope entry status/completion), and never creates a retirement checkpoint or rewrites archive/. Added COMPLETION_CONFLICT and NOT_READY_TO_COMPLETE error codes, scope_complete to GuardedOperation/default policy, mutating-invocation wiring in app.ts, help documentation, cloneScopeEntry completion preservation in state.ts, and end-to-end regression coverage in check-scope-retire.mjs (refuses active sprint/debt, dry-run, unconfirmed, happy apply, double-complete conflict, status/context-pack visibility).

checked_criteria: An eligible open scope can be explicitly completed only through the dedicated tool-owned scope transition with confirmation.
The transition refuses non-ready or divergent scopes with no state write.
Completion is visible in status and context-pack and remains structurally distinct from retirement.

phases.title: Deliberate continuation and certification
phases.objective: Allow a completed-but-not-retired scope to resume planning explicitly, then prove the lifecycle boundaries end to end.

tasks.title: Implement explicit scope reopen for later planning
tasks.description: Add an auditable reopen transition for a completed, non-retired scope so new work can return to plan_sprint without manual state edits or recovery.
tasks.context: Reopen is not retirement reversal and cannot modify immutable close archives. Preserve completion history and require a non-empty reason. A retired scope remains terminal and is never reopened by this path.
acceptance_criteria: A completed non-retired scope can be explicitly reopened with an auditable reason and then plan a later sprint normally.
Reopen refuses retired, active, malformed, or already-open scopes without writes.
Completion history remains visible after reopening and all existing archives keep identical bytes.

evidence.summary: Added tool-owned 'kyro scope reopen': an explicitly completed, non-retired scope returns to plan_sprint under one locked, digest-bound, resumable transaction that clears the live completion and preserves it in append-only completionHistory (sprint.json + registry). Shared after-state builders (checkpoints/lifecycle-state.ts) are now the single source of truth for both writers and for checkpoint verification, which replays recorded lifecycle transitions from the close after-image instead of trusting the records — closing the divergence hole that made a completed or reopened scope read as tampered.
validation: npm run check (full suite, exit 0) including typecheck, dist freshness, and every contract script

node scripts/check-scope-retire.mjs: new reopen contract — happy path, plan-after-reopen (S3/S7), refusals for open/retired/malformed/unknown/second-reopen without writes, dry-run and CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, fault-injected resume (KYRO_TEST_REOPEN_FAIL_AFTER=sprint) and DIVERGED on concurrent registry edit
archive/ byte digest asserted identical across completion, reopen, planning, resume, and every refusal path

checked_criteria: A completed non-retired scope can be explicitly reopened with an auditable reason and then plan a later sprint normally.
Reopen refuses retired, active, malformed, or already-open scopes without writes.
Completion history remains visible after reopening and all existing archives keep identical bytes.

tasks.title: Certify completion, reopen, and integrity boundaries
tasks.description: Extend existing lifecycle and integrity gates with end-to-end adversarial cases and update only the user-facing guidance required by the final contract.
tasks.context: Do not create a new test harness. Prove explicit completion differs from retirement, explicit reopen permits planning, and unsafe artifacts or stale requests stay fail-closed for the affected scope.
acceptance_criteria: Focused end-to-end gates fail when completion is inferred from roadmap exhaustion or when reopen silently bypasses its preconditions.
Retirement remains human-gated and terminal while completion and reopening are independently observable.
npm run check, Doctor, analyze, Integrity prepare, and package dry-run pass after the changes.

evidence.summary: Extended the existing gates (no new harness) with adversarial S4 coverage and updated the user-facing contract. check-scope-retire now proves lawful lifecycle evolution stays healthy and is labelled 'explicit lifecycle transition', that completing again after a reopen replays correctly, and that state edited beyond a transition, a rewritten lifecycle record, or a corrupt immutable narrative each still fail closed as DIVERGED. check-status adds the reopen derivation model plus malformed/empty/out-of-order history rejection; check-plan adds the refusal that stops planning from bypassing completion (remedy names reopen; a retired scope is never offered it); check-close-handoff asserts close never mints completion, history, or retirement. docs/cli.md and docs/status-coherence.md document the three distinct lifecycle facts and the replay-based verification.
validation: npm run check: exit 0 (full suite, including typecheck, dist freshness, and all contract scripts)
node dist/cli.js doctor --artifacts --kyro-scope adaptive-sprint-lifecycle: all PASS, exit 0
node dist/cli.js analyze --kyro-scope adaptive-sprint-lifecycle: no semantic issues, exit 0
node dist/cli.js repair integrity prepare --json: no findings, no blockers, exit 0

checked_criteria: Focused end-to-end gates fail when completion is inferred from roadmap exhaustion or when reopen silently bypasses its preconditions.
Retirement remains human-gated and terminal while completion and reopening are independently observable.
npm run check, Doctor, analyze, Integrity prepare, and package dry-run pass after the changes.

emergentTasks.title: Make scope completion atomic and recoverable
emergentTasks.description: Repair the scope-complete writer so all preconditions and both state updates share one writer lease, failed intermediate application resumes safely, and conflicting state fails closed.
emergentTasks.context: Corrective work for QA Major: scope completion must match Kyro's lock/CAS recovery guarantees without a new root verb or retirement checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Completion revalidates sprint and project state inside one state-writer lock before any write.
A failure after sprint write resumes the exact same completion request without overwriting divergent state.
Conflicting request or concurrent state mutation fails closed and no archive bytes change.

evidence.summary: Made scope completion a locked, recoverable transition and reject digest-only false success.
validation: Doctor, analyze, and scoped integrity prepare

checked_criteria: Completion revalidates sprint and project state inside one state-writer lock before any write.

Conflicting request or concurrent state mutation fails closed and no archive bytes change.

definitionOfDone: Scope completion, reopening, and retirement have distinct typed transitions and rendered states.
No ordinary sprint close infers completion or blocks lawful future planning.
All new lifecycle transitions are tool-owned, fail closed on invalid state, and preserve immutable archives.
Focused lifecycle regressions and the full project validation suite pass.
